questions.text: The local administration system of the Cholas is considered a model for modern “Gram Swarajya.” Justify this statement.
questions.text_as_printed: The local administration system of the Cholas is considered a model for modern “Gram Swarajya.” Justify this statement. (D)

answer.value: The Cholas granted complete autonomy to village assemblies such as the Mahasabha and the Ur to manage local affairs. They implemented an organized electoral system (Kudavolai) with strict eligibility criteria related to property ownership and education. Separate committees looked after important village infrastructure such as irrigation tanks, gardens, and temples, ensuring self-sufficiency at the grassroots level.

questions.text: Vishnuvardhana the King of Hoysala was an exceptional ruler. Substantiate the statement.
questions.text_as_printed: Vishnuvardhana the King of Hoysala was an exceptional ruler. Substantiate the statement. (D)

answer.value:
Hoysala Contributions:
Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana conquered Gangavadi and earned the title Talakadugonda.
To commemorate his victories, he built the Keertinarayana Temple in Talakad and the Chennakeshava Temple in Belur.
His efforts to expand the empire were thwarted by Chalukya king Vikramaditya VI.
Ramanujacharya, unable to propagate Vishishtadvaita in the Chola kingdom, sought refuge under Bittideva and spread it across Karnataka.
General Ketu Malla built the Hoysaleshwara and Shantaleshwara temples in Halebidu.
Many Jain basadis and temples were constructed during this period

questions.text: Explain in detail the contributions of the Hoysalas to the field of literature.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain in detail the contributions of the Hoysalas to the field of literature. (D)

answer.value:
During the Hoysala period, literature flourished remarkably. They patronized scholars of Kannada, Sanskrit, and Tamil.
Famous Kannada poets enriched the language: Janna wrote Yashodhara Charite, Harihara wrote Girija Kalyana, and Raghavanka wrote Harishchandra Kavya.
The grammarian Keshiraja wrote the outstanding Kannada grammar work Shabdamanidarpana.
Ramanujacharya, a famous philosopher, made immense contributions to Sanskrit religious and philosophical literature.

questions.text: Explain the contributions of the Cholas to art and architecture.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the contributions of the Cholas to art and architecture. (A)

answer.value:
The Cholas were Shaivites and built many Shiva temples.
The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur stands in a vast courtyard measuring 500 feet in length and 250 feet in width. Its tower (shikhara) is 200 feet high.
The Choleswara temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram built by Rajendra, the Choleswara temple at Begur near Aprameya (near Channapatna), and the Mukeshwara temple at Bennamangala in Karnataka served as economic and cultural centers.
During their period, the idols of Shiva, Ganapati, Vishnu, Durga, and Kartikeya became famous.

questions.text: Explain the features of art and architecture during the Hoysala period.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the features of art and architecture during the Hoysala period. (D)

answer.value:
Hoysala sculpture is world-famous. The Hoysalas built numerous temples using soft soapstone.
Their temples have five main features: star-shaped sanctum (garbhagriha), raised platform (jagati), wall decorations, and ornate pillars and towers.
The Chennakeshava Temple at Belur has beautifully carved Madanikas on its pillars. The Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu was built by the commander Ketamalla.
The Keshava Temple at Somanathapura, built by Somadandanayaka, is also famous.
Apart from these, there are many temples at places like Arasikere, Govindanahalli, Doddagaddavalli, and Bhadravati. All these are known for their extremely intricate carvings and have left a lasting impact on architecture.
